name: KTTKS
lead: KTTKS is a pentapeptide (lysine-threonine-threonine-lysine-serine) used in anti-wrinkle skin care, usually in its palmitoylated form, palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 (Pal-KTTKS), sold under the trade name Matrixyl. Sederma launched Matrixyl in 2000. It is classed as a matrikine, a messenger peptide that regulates cell activity [8][9].

It was designed as a topical agent to stimulate collagen production. In a 12-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled, split-face study of 93 women aged 35 to 55, pal-KTTKS was assessed for improvement in photoaged facial skin [1]. Laboratory work shows C16-KTTKS stimulates collagen production in human fibroblasts [3]. Questions about how well the peptide penetrates skin are discussed in the literature [6][7].

paras: KTTKS is a cosmetic ingredient aimed at wrinkles and photoaged skin. The 16-carbon palmitoyl chain is intended to help the molecule cross the skin's lipid layers [8].

Wikipedia describes the peptide as activating the synthesis of extracellular matrix macromolecules, linking this to its anti-wrinkle effect [8]. In vitro, C16-KTTKS stimulated collagen production in human dermal and corneal fibroblasts in a concentration-dependent manner, close to the concentration at which it self-assembles into nanotape structures [3]. Related work found KTTKS increased type I collagen and TGF-beta expression in tendon cells [10].

Studies have examined stability and permeation of KTTKS and palmitoyl-KTTKS in skin [7], microneedle-enhanced delivery of cosmeceutical peptides [2], and the argument that skin permeability is a necessary consideration for anti-wrinkle peptide performance [6]. Reviews of topical KTTKS are available [9].

A 12-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled, split-face, left-right randomized study in 93 Caucasian female subjects aged 35 to 55 compared pal-KTTKS-containing formulations with comparators for photoaged facial skin, and was reported as showing improvement [1]. The study design used the peptide's collagen-stimulating rationale [1]. The sources reviewed do not describe independent replication in this summary, and a 2011 review discusses topical KTTKS evidence overall [9].
Matrixyl and related peptides are marketed in cosmetic products. The sources reviewed contain no looksmaxxing community discussion of KTTKS.

timeline.event: Clinical study of pal-KTTKS in photoaged facial skin published [1].

card.summary: The collagen-signalling pentapeptide behind Matrixyl, with a modest split-face trial and open questions about skin penetration.
card.note: Skin penetration is debated in the literature.

quick.overview:
KTTKS is a five-amino-acid peptide, usually attached to a palmitoyl fat chain and sold as Matrixyl in anti-wrinkle products since 2000.

A 93-subject double-blind split-face study of pal-KTTKS in photoaged facial skin reported improvement, and lab studies show it raises collagen production in cultured cells.
quick.mechanism: It is a matrikine, reported to stimulate extracellular matrix and collagen synthesis in skin cells; the fat chain is meant to aid penetration.
quick.risks: The sources reviewed do not report safety problems. Reviewers discuss whether enough peptide reaches the dermis, and it is sold as a cosmetic ingredient.
